events.title: Lewis and Clark Resume Their Journey West
events.description: The Corps of Discovery broke camp among the Mandan people in present-day North Dakota. It continued up the Missouri River into territory unknown to the United States.
events.significance: The expedition's westward push produced the first detailed American maps, and scientific and cultural records, of the American interior.

events.title: The Battle of Shiloh Ends
events.description: After two days of fighting near Shiloh, Tennessee, Union forces under Ulysses S. Grant defeated the Confederate army. Fresh reinforcements helped turn the tide.
events.significance: The battle's staggering casualties shattered hopes of a short Civil War. It also strengthened Union control of the western theater.

events.title: Beer Returns as Prohibition Begins to Unravel
events.description: Beer of no more than 3.2% alcohol by weight became legal again in the United States. This came months before Prohibition was formally repealed.
events.significance: It was the first public step in dismantling Prohibition. It marked a major shift in American law and daily life.

events.title: The World Health Organization Is Founded
events.description: The World Health Organization officially came into being as a specialized agency of the United Nations. Its constitution took effect on this date.
events.significance: The WHO has led global efforts against disease, including the campaign that eradicated smallpox. April 7 is now marked each year as World Health Day.

events.title: The Rwandan Genocide Begins
events.description: Beginning on April 7, 1994, Rwanda's government-backed extremists launched about 100 days of mass killing. Their targets were Tutsi and moderate Hutu political figures.
events.significance: Over a million people were killed. The genocide remains a harsh lesson about hate speech, international inaction, and the duty to prevent atrocities.
